answer: The oasis issued its trade tokens from a vault behind the kiln: clay stamped wet is worthless, so every token was fired until it rings when tapped — a test anyone can run with a knuckle. Cargoes reaching the wharf showed a fired token per crate; forgers who stamped soft clay watched their goods refused when the first tap went thud, and the vault replaced only tokens whose ring matched its firing log. Standing here is ceramic, not printed: it survives the tap or it doesn't exist.
